title: A primitive fixed vector over a DVR has a scalar endomorphism detector
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and algebraically closed residue field $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$. Let $H$ be a smooth affine finitely presented group scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with the group-object diagrams over this base. Suppose $H$ is split semisimple simply connected: its geometric fibres are connected and have no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, every central isogeny onto such a fibre from a connected semisimple group is an isomorphism, and it has a split maximal torus and a Borel subgroup scheme containing it. Here a central isogeny is a surjective group homomorphism with finite central kernel; solvable means that the iterated derived subgroups eventually become trivial; a split torus is a group scheme isomorphic to a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$; maximal tori and Borel subgroup schemes have, on each geometric fibre, a maximal torus and a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup, respectively. A rational $H$-module is an $A$-module $M$ with $A$-linear coaction $M\to M\otimes_A A[H]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities, where $A[H]=\Gamma(H,\mathcal O_H)$ has the coordinate Hopf algebra maps; fixed vectors satisfy $\rho(m)=m\otimes1$. Equivariance means commutation with coactions. Tensor and dual modules have diagonal and contragredient coactions. Write $\operatorname{Sym}^n_A M$ for the degree-$n$ part of the commutative algebra freely generated by $M$, with the induced coaction. Let $V$ be a finite free rational $H$-module and $v\in V^H$ primitive, meaning $v\notin\mathfrak mV$. There exist a nonzero finite free rational $H$-module $W$ and an equivariant $A$-linear map $\phi:V\to\operatorname{End}_A(W)$, where $H$ acts on endomorphisms by conjugation, such that the scalar map $A\to\operatorname{End}_A(W)^H$, $a\mapsto a\,\mathrm{id}_W$, is an isomorphism of $A$-modules and the reduction of $\phi(v)$ in $\operatorname{End}_\kappa(W\otimes_A\kappa)$ is nonzero. Finite free means having a finite basis, and nonzero means positive rank.

source.place: Lemmas 9.7.2(1),(2), Remark 9.7.3, Lemma 9.7.4 and their combination in Theorem 9.7.5, printed pp.526--528. proof.text: Fix the split torus and Borel from the hypotheses. By [lem-sfb-dvr-rho-section-modules], choose $\rho,\widetilde\rho$ and the actual left-translation modules $W_m$, which are finite free of positive rank for every $m\ge1$. All subsequent maps are maps of rational $H$-modules over $A$.

source.place: Theorem 9.7.5, endomorphism construction, printed pp.527--528; Lemmas 9.7.2 and 9.7.4. Primary PDF read online; basis calculations supplied by Q59.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-rho-tensor-square-eventual-detection] to the given finite free $V$ and primitive fixed $v$, obtaining a threshold $M$. If $\operatorname{char}\kappa=0$, take $m=M$; if $\operatorname{char}\kappa=p>0$, choose $r\ge1$ with $p^r-1\ge M$ and take $m=p^r-1$. These weights are unbounded since $p\ge2$. Put $W=W_m$. Detection gives $a:V\to W\otimes_A W$ with nonzero residual value at $v$; [lem-sfb-dvr-rho-section-self-duality] gives an equivariant isomorphism $j:W\simeq W^\vee$ at this same weight.

source.place: Theorem 9.7.5, endomorphism construction, printed pp.527--528; Lemmas 9.7.2 and 9.7.4. Primary PDF read online; basis calculations supplied by Q59.

proof.text: Define $\theta:W\otimes_A W^\vee\to\operatorname{End}_A(W)$ by $\theta(w\otimes\ell)(z)=\ell(z)w$. In a finite basis $(e_i)$, its inverse is $T\mapsto\sum_iT(e_i)\otimes e_i^\vee$; the two composite identities follow by expanding $z=\sum_i e_i^\vee(z)e_i$. After every scalar extension, $\theta(hw\otimes h\ell)(z)=\ell(h^{-1}z)hw=(h\theta(w\otimes\ell)h^{-1})(z)$, so $\theta$ is equivariant. Thus $\phi=\theta(1\otimes j)a$ is equivariant. The inverse formulas also remain inverses after tensoring with $\kappa$, and identify $\operatorname{End}_A(W)\otimes_A\kappa$ with $\operatorname{End}_\kappa(W\otimes_A\kappa)$ by matrix entries. Consequently $\phi(v)$ has nonzero reduction.

source.place: Theorem 9.7.5, endomorphism construction, printed pp.527--528; Lemmas 9.7.2 and 9.7.4. Primary PDF read online; basis calculations supplied by Q59.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-dvr-rho-tensor-square-invariant-line], $(W\otimes_A W)^H$ is free of rank one. The equivariant isomorphism $\theta(1\otimes j)$ and its equivariant inverse restrict to inverse maps of invariant submodules. Hence $N=\operatorname{End}_A(W)^H$ is free of rank one.

source.place: Theorem 9.7.5, endomorphism construction, printed pp.527--528; Lemmas 9.7.2 and 9.7.4. Primary PDF read online; basis calculations supplied by Q59.

proof.text: Choose a generator $T$ of $N$ and write $\mathrm{id}_W=bT$. There is a diagonal entry because $W$ has positive rank; that entry gives $1=bT_{ii}$ in $A$. Thus $b$ is a unit and $T=b^{-1}\mathrm{id}_W$, so every invariant endomorphism is scalar. If $c\,\mathrm{id}_W=0$, a diagonal entry gives $c=0$. The scalar map is therefore injective and surjective, and is $A$-linear by its formula. Together with the nonzero residual value from step 3, this proves every conclusion.

Step 4 transports invariants through an equivariant iso with equivariant inverse. Step 5's diagonal-entry argument makes b a unit.
